instruction: Select all images containing a bicycle.

game.semantic_variant: Select all vehicles powered by pedals.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary bicycles count, and so do the bicycle with hexagonal wheels and the bicycle carrying six saddles: impossible, but still bicycles. The exercise bike, the horse with pedals and the pedal-powered office chair are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The rocking horse and the motorcycle are not bicycles.

correct: Your understanding of bicycles has been noted.
All bicycles accounted for. A copy has been placed on file.
Correct. The square-wheeled bicycle has been recognised. Its roadworthiness has not.
Correct. All six saddles have been accounted for.
partial: Partially correct. Your relationship with bicycles will be reviewed.
Some bicycles escaped your attention. They have been informed.
incorrect: Incorrect. The bicycles have asked not to be contacted further.
Incorrect. The Department is not angry about the bicycles, merely disappointed.

selection_review.reason: Version 2 of C01, completing the composition of prompt 007: two ordinary bicycles, two impossible bicycles, three borderline cases and two clear non-members. Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary bicycles (orange and teal mountain bike on grass, three-quarter view; red vintage bicycle against a blue wall, side view), two impossible bicycles (lavender bicycle edited to roll on hexagonal wheels; navy road bicycle edited to carry six leather saddles), three borderline cases (recumbent exercise bike, generated chestnut horse with bicycle parts, generated pedal-powered office chair) and two non-members (rocking horse, motorcycle). The kick scooter of version 1 is dropped to make room for the second impossible bicycle. Colours (orange, red, lavender, navy, grey, chestnut), views and settings vary within each role; no view, colour or setting singles out the targets.
